settings.name_in_paper: One-point bandit feedback with tree-compatible losses (lower bound)
unmapped: Actions are leaves of a known depth-L rooted tree; losses are tree-compatible: |y_t(a)-y_t(b)| <= sigma_{s(a,b)} with nonincreasing scales sigma_j

Nested loss model of Martin et al. (2022): node losses ell_t(v) in [0, R_j] for v at level j, action loss is sum of node losses along root-to-leaf path; learner observes all node losses on the path of the chosen action
Tree structure and weights R_j known to the learner
Regret is E[sum y_t(A_t)] - min_a E[sum y_t(a)]; losses may depend on the past but not on the current action
settings.definition_quote: the adversary selects at every round a function $\ell_t \colon \cV \rightarrow [0,1]$ assigning a loss to every node in the tree such that $\ell_t(v) \leq R_j$ for all $v \in V_j$ ... the learner gets to observe all the values $(\ell_t(v))_{\ancof{v}{a}}$ upon choosing $A_t = a$.

settings.name_in_paper: Full-path (nested semi-bandit) feedback, generalized stochastic setting (Condition 1)
unmapped: Nested loss model with node losses in [0,R_j] and full-path feedback
Condition 1: exists Delta in R^K_+ with at most one zero entry such that Reg >= E sum Delta(A_t) for any algorithm (C = 0 self-bounding)
settings.definition_quote: There exists a vector $\Delta \in \R^K_+$ satisfying $|\{a\in \cA \colon \Delta(a)=0\}| \leq 1$ such that $\reg{T}{m} \geq \E \sum_{t=1}^T \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m\Delta(A_{t,i})$ holds for any algorithm.

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-point (2 to L+1 point) bandit feedback with tree-compatible losses, adversarial regime
unmapped: Learner plays m actions per round, observes all their losses and pays their average loss (no free exploration)
Tree-compatible losses |y_t(a)-y_t(b)| <= sigma_{s(a,b)}; tree and scales sigma_j known to the learner
Regret E[avg loss] - min_a E[sum y_t(a)]; losses can depend on the past but not on current actions
settings.definition_quote: At every round $t$, the environment secretly draws a tree-compatible loss function $y_t$, and simultaneously, the learner plays $m\ge 1$ actions $A_{t,1},\dots,A_{t, m}\in\cA$, observes $y_t(A_{t,1}),\dots,y_t(A_{t,m})$, and incurs their average $\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m y_t(A_{t,i})$.

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-point bandit feedback with tree-compatible losses, generalized stochastic setting (Condition 1)
unmapped: Learner plays m actions per round, observes all their losses and pays their average loss
Tree-compatible losses with known scales sigma_j
Condition 1 (generalized stochastic setting with gap vector Delta, at most one zero entry)
settings.definition_quote: There exists a vector $\Delta \in \R^K_+$ satisfying $|\{a\in \cA \colon \Delta(a)=0\}| \leq 1$ such that $\reg{T}{m} \geq \E \sum_{t=1}^T \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m\Delta(A_{t,i})$ holds for any algorithm.

settings.name_in_paper: Metric (Lipschitz) bandits with two-point feedback (general metric d_{A,infty})
unmapped: Losses 1-Lipschitz w.r.t. the induced metric d_{A,infty}(a,b)=sup over admissible losses |l(a)-l(b)|; learner uses nested covers of the action set (known metric)
Two actions played per round, regret on their average loss
settings.definition_quote: suppose we are now given an arbitrary action set $\actions$ and a set $\losses$ of admissible loss functions ... $d_{\actions,\infty}(a, b) \coloneqq \sup_{\loss \in \losses} |\loss(a) - \loss(b)|$

settings.name_in_paper: Lipschitz bandits on a compact subset of R^d with two-point feedback
unmapped: Action set is a compact subset of R^d with Euclidean diameter D; losses G-Lipschitz; two actions played per round and their average loss is paid
settings.definition_quote: let $\actions \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact set with diameter $D$ (\wrt to the Euclidean metric), and let $\losses$ be the set of $G$-Lipschitz loss functions from $\actions$ to $\R$.

algorithms.name: FTRL with nested 1/2-Tsallis regularizer and semi-bandit feedback (Algorithm 3)

source.label: prop:one-point-tree-lb
source.quote: Let $\rho\coloneqq \scale_L$. For $K>2$, $T>32(K-1)\log(14)$, and $\rho > 0.22\sqrt{(K-1)/T}$, any randomized one-point bandit algorithm satisfies \sup_{(y_t)_{t=1}^T \in \cY^T_\scale}\ \E\!\left[\reg{T}{1}(y_{1:T})\right] \;>\; \frac{1}{504}\sqrt{T(K-1)}.

results.notes: Strict inequality (>). Direct reduction to Gerchinovitz & Lattimore (2016) Corollary 4. Sup over loss sequences in the class; strict lower bound.

symbols.K_eff_R: effective number of actions (sum_j R_j sqrt(|V_j|))^2, V_j the nodes at level j

conditions: node losses ell_t(v) in [0, R_j] for v in V_j
tuning: psi_t(p) = sqrt(5 max{t,20}) sum_j R_j sum_{v in V_j} (p[v] - sqrt(p[v]))

source.label: thm:semi-bandit-feedback
source.quote: FTRL with $\psi_t(p) = \sqrt{ 5 \max\{t, 20\} } \sum_{j \in [L]} R_j \sum_{v \in V_j} p[v] - \sqrt{p[v]}$ and $z_t(a) = \sum_{\ancof{v}{a}} \indicator{\ancof{v}{A_t}} {\ell_t(v)} /{p_t[v]}$ satisfies $\reg{T}{1} \leq 15 \sqrt{\keff(R)} + 4 \sqrt{5  \keff(R) T }$ ...

results.notes: Learning rate does not depend on T, so anytime. Data-dependent intermediate bound (Proposition prop:semi-bandit-feedback) not recorded separately.

symbols.K_sto_R: (sum_j R_j sqrt(Gamma(j,Delta)))^2 with Gamma(j,Delta)=sum over level-j nodes v with nonzero min descendant gap of 1/min_{a desc of v} Delta(a)

tuning: psi_t(p) = sqrt(5 max{t,20}) sum_j R_j sum_{v in V_j} (p[v] - sqrt(p[v]))
psi_t(p) = 2 sqrt(6) sum_j (sigma_j/sqrt(delta_j)) sqrt(max{t, 6/delta_j}) sum_{v in V_j} (x[v]-sqrt(x[v]))

source.label: thm:2-point-feedback
source.quote: \Cref{alg:2-point-feedback} with $ \psi_t(p) = 2\sqrt{6} \sum_{j \in [L]} (\scale_j/\sqrt{\delta_j})  \sqrt{\max\bcb{t, {6}/{\delta_j}}} \sum_{v \in V_j} x[v] - \sqrt{x[v]}$ and $b_\lvl = \scale_\lvl$ for all $\lvl \in [L]$ satisfies $\reg{T}{2} \leq 18 \sqrt{\keff(\sigma/{\delta})} + 8 \sqrt{6}  \sqrt{\keff(\sigma/\sqrt{\delta}) T}$ ...

results.notes: Paper notes the bound extends to m-point feedback with delta_j the probability level j is chosen; uniform delta gives extra sqrt(L) factor.

symbols.xi_j: probability that level j is among the sampled levels

tuning: psi_t(x) = 4 sqrt(c)/sqrt(c-1) sum_j (sigma_j/sqrt(xi_j)) max{sqrt(t), sqrt(c(c-1)/xi_j)} sum_{v in V_j}(x[v]-sqrt(x[v]))

source.label: thm:n-point-feedback
source.quote: \Cref{alg:n-point-feedback} with $\psi_t$ ... where $c \geq 2$, and $b_\lvl = \scale_\lvl$ for all $\lvl \in [L]$ satisfies \reg{T}{n+1} \leq 6c \sum_{j \in [L]} \frac{\scale_j}{ \xi_j} \sqrt{|V_j|} + \frac{16 \sqrt{c}}{\sqrt{(c-1)}} \sum_{j \in [L]} \frac{\scale_j}{\sqrt{\xi_j}} \sqrt{|V_j| T}.

results.notes: Multi-point (n+1 point) feedback mapped to two_point feedback vocabulary. Uniform level sampling without replacement gives sqrt(L/n) scaling.

symbols.xi_j: probability that level j is among the sampled levels

source.label: thm:n-point-feedback
source.quote: Further, if \Cref{condition:stochastic} holds, then, \Cref{alg:n-point-feedback} also satisfies \reg{T}{n+1} \leq  12 c \sum_{j \in [L]} \frac{\scale_j}{ \xi_j} \sqrt{|V_j|} + \frac{64 c}{c-1} \Bbrb{ \sum_{j \in [L]} \frac{\scale_j}{\sqrt{\xi_j}} \sqrt{ \Gamma(j,\Delta) }}^2 \ln(eT).

results.notes: Proof of the stochastic part says it proceeds similarly to Theorem semi.
